changed.title: A batch of two-name calibrations can retain exactly one measured bit per raw key bit
changed.unlocks: retains the full calibration in exactly nk binary measurements across n independent keys
changed.context: The reply difference is affine. Select independent coordinate rows and call its kernel T. The mixer kernel K has index two in T. Choose a lift t in T outside K. The baseline change along t ranges in an affine space disjoint from the final rotation of K by injectivity. Pick a functional zero on that rotated kernel and one on the affine space. Add s-1 parities distinguishing points of the kernel. This resolves each difference fiber. Repeat per key. A smaller budget cannot exist because a batch fiber has 2^(ns) keys. Allow 95 to 170 minutes.

changed.title: Some pair of fixed row names identifies every raw key exactly at widths other than one and three
changed.statement:
∀ (k : Nat) (hk : 0 < k),
  let W := Fin k → Bool
  let ix := fun (i : Nat) => (⟨i % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let add := fun (u v : W) (i : Fin k) => xor (u i) (v i)
  let mix := fun (d : Nat) (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    xor (x (ix (i.val+k-d % k))) (xor (x i) (x (ix (i.val+d))))
  let rot := fun (a : Nat) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (ix (i.val+k-a % k))
  let chi := fun (r : W) (i : Fin k) => xor (r i) (!(r (ix (i.val+1))) && r (ix (i.val+2)))
  let row := fun (name x : W) => add (chi (mix 1 (add name (rot 1 x)))) x
  let m := 1 + (k-1) % 3
  (∀ q : Nat, (∃ names : Fin q → W, Function.Injective (fun x : W => fun j : Fin q => row (names j) x)) ↔
    k ≠ 1 ∧ k ≠ 3 ∧ 2 ≤ q) ∧
  ((k = 2 ∨ 4 ≤ k) → ∃ v : W,
    (∀ i : Fin k, mix 1 v i = (if k = 2 then decide (i.val = 1) else decide (m ≤ i.val))) ∧
    ∀ u : W, Function.Injective (fun x : W => (row u x, row (add u v) x)))
changed.unlocks: identifies the entire unknown raw key using a suitable fixed pair of row names even at singular mixer widths
changed.context: Let N be the mixed name difference. A collision forces the mixed key difference B to be constant on the run of ones and zero at adjacent zeros. For three zeros the residue sums force the middle bit of B to vanish. The only nonzero possibility is N. Then the baseline fixes the raw difference. With one or two zeros its boundary bits contradict the cyclic recurrence. With three zeros the baseline forces unequal residue sums of the mixed key. A one-name calibration cannot exist because the cancelling key and its complement collide. Allow 120 to 210 minutes.

changed.title: Fitting optimal fan-in-two AND/OR equality on positive triples and arbitrary negatives admits relative counts at all sizes via deletion to bipartiteness
changed.statement:
let header := fun j : Nat => List.replicate j true ++ [false]
let fast := fun f : List Bool → List Bool =>
  ∃ M : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => x) (fun x : List Bool => x) f,
    ∀ i, Finite (M.tm.Γ i)

let frame := fun j : Nat => j.bits.flatMap (fun b => [true,b]) ++ [false]
∃ (count : List Bool → List Bool) (d : Nat), fast count ∧
∀ (n : Nat), 2 ≤ n →
  ∀ (pos : List (Finset (Fin n))) (neg : List (Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n))),
  let ends := fun e : Fin n × Fin n => ({e.1,e.2} : Finset (Fin n))
  let E := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)).filter (fun e => e.1 < e.2 ∧
    ∀ z ∈ neg, ¬(ends e ⊆ z.1) ∧ ¬(ends e ⊆ z.2))
  let proper := fun (X : Finset (Fin n)) (side : Fin n → Bool) =>
    ∀ e ∈ E, e.1 ∉ X → e.2 ∉ X → side e.1 ≠ side e.2
  (∀ R ∈ pos, ∀ e ∈ E, ends e ⊆ R → ∀ f ∈ E, ends f ⊆ R →
    ¬Disjoint (ends e) (ends f)) →
  let Fn := (Fin n → Bool) → (Fin n → Bool) → Bool
  let obs := fun (f : Fn) (R S : Finset (Fin n)) =>
    f (fun i => decide (i ∈ R)) (fun j => decide (j ∈ S))
  let fits := fun f : Fn => (∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size+1 ≤ 2*n ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun i j : Fin n => decide (i=j)) C ∧
    ∀ x y, f x y = C.eval (List.ofFn x ++ List.ofFn y)) ∧
    (∀ R ∈ pos, obs f R ∅ = true) ∧ (∀ z ∈ neg, obs f z.1 z.2 = false)

  let size := fun f : Fn => (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : Fin n × Fin n =>
    z.1 < z.2 ∧ obs f {z.1,z.2} ∅ = true)).card
  let hist := fun s : Nat => Nat.card {f : Fn // fits f ∧ size f = s}

  let bank := fun R : Finset (Fin n) => (List.finRange n).map (fun i => decide (i ∈ R))
  let input := header n ++ header pos.length ++ pos.flatMap bank ++
    header neg.length ++ neg.flatMap (fun z => bank z.1 ++ bank z.2)

  ∀ (q b a : Nat), 2 ≤ b → 1 ≤ a →
    let possible := ∃ (X : Finset (Fin n)) (side : Fin n → Bool), X.card ≤ q ∧ proper X side
    let prefixBits := header q ++ header b ++ header a ++ input
    let ell := 2^(d*(q+1)) * (prefixBits.length+2)^d
    let out := fun tape : Fin ell → Bool => count (prefixBits ++ List.ofFn tape)
    (∀ tape, out tape = [] ↔ ¬possible) ∧
    (possible → ∃ (X : Finset (Fin n)) (side : Fin n → Bool),
      X.card ≤ q ∧ proper X side ∧
      ∃ z : (Fin ell → Bool) → Fin (n/2+1) → Nat,
        (∀ tape, out tape = bank X ++ List.ofFn side ++
          (List.finRange (n/2+1)).flatMap (fun s => frame (z tape s))) ∧
        (∀ tape s, z tape s = 0 ↔ hist s.val = 0) ∧
        2^a * Nat.card {tape : Fin ell → Bool // ∀ s : Fin (n/2+1),
          (4*b-4)*hist s.val ≤ z tape s ∧ z tape s ≤ (4*b+4)*hist s.val} ≥ (2^a-1)*2^ell)
changed.unlocks: Gives a computable deletion certificate, exact zero bins and simultaneous relative counts, including maximum size. The scaled integer z denotes z/(4b).
changed.context: Find a deletion set by odd-cycle transversal compression and two-color its complement. For each extension and size, test the support matrix for a perfect matching, then approximate each positive permanent by Jerrum, Sinclair and Vigoda. Sum the nonnegative estimates and divide by the exact color and factorial factors. Allocate failure over all branches and sizes, then round once to the integer z representing z/(4b). Exact support tests determine every zero, and one deterministic certificate works on all tapes. The budget is tested before inspecting fit feasibility.

changed.title: The independence number of marked endpoints determines the NOT budget for vertex cover with parity outputs
changed.statement:
∀ n : Nat, ∀ G H : Finset (Fin n × Fin n),
  (∀ e ∈ G, e.1 < e.2) → H ⊆ G →
  let active := H.image Prod.fst ∪ H.image Prod.snd
  let independent := fun S : Finset (Fin n) =>
    S ⊆ active ∧ ∀ e ∈ G, ¬(e.1 ∈ S ∧ e.2 ∈ S)
  let cover := fun x : Fin n → Bool => ∀ e ∈ G, x e.1=true ∨ x e.2=true
  ∀ r : Nat,
    (∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
        (tap : ↥H → Fin (n+2+C.size)),
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n+2) C ∧
      C.output < n+2+C.size ∧ PEqualNP.NotBracket.notCount C ≤ r ∧
      ∀ x : Fin n → Bool,
        let inputs := List.ofFn x ++ [false,true]
        (C.eval inputs = true ↔ cover x) ∧
        (cover x → ∀ e, (C.wires inputs).getD (tap e).val false = xor (x e.val.1) (x e.val.2))) ↔
    ∀ S : Finset (Fin n), independent S → S.card < 2^r
changed.unlocks: Gives a common inversion budget for all marked-edge witness circuits while leaving their total gate costs open.
changed.context: Fill the zero vertices of an independent set one at a time. At every step some marked edge loses its parity signal. A circuit with r negations has at most two to the power r minus one downward steps on an increasing chain. For the construction, give each cover the rank alpha minus its number of zeros among marked endpoints. Read the rank bits from high to low. On covers augmented by earlier bits and their complements, the next bit has a monotone extension. Negate it once. At equal rank comparable covers agree on every marked endpoint, so each parity has a monotone extension.

changed.sketch: Exploration of one NOT on an eight-vertex graph. Test an AND/OR witness against all 256 inputs, then prove that shorter circuits with at most one NOT fail using a gate lower bound or an exhaustive certificate. For a saving, exhibit the one-NOT circuit and exclude every shorter or equal-sized AND/OR circuit. The graph reader will inspect the shared wires and the input of the NOT in each saving. An equality removes this graph from the search for a saving.
